summary: Generation stall leading to client-side timeout for ultra-long prefix + large max_tokens
description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports repeated client-side timeouts and stalled streaming when sending prompts with an ultra-long prefix (~120k tokens) together with a large max_tokens (>=60k). The generation appears to start (initial tokens returned) then stalls for an extended period (~60–120s) before the client receives either a socket close or an HTTP 504. This is reproducible in prod for the customer on dedicated capacity.

Impact:
- Customer's batch jobs for document summarization fail ~40% of runs when using extended prefix + high max_tokens.
- End-users see partial outputs or timeouts; jobs must be retried, increasing cost.

Environment:
- Customer: PolarisAI (dedicated account)
- Region: us-west primary, some runs in us-east also affected
- Models: rwd-adapter-gpt-extended-7B (primary), rwd-adapter-gptx-13B (fallback)
- Platform: Dedicated pool (c5-gpu-4), API via production gateway, streaming enabled

Steps to reproduce (customer-provided):
1) Construct a prompt with a ~120k-token prefix (multiple concatenated documents).
2) Call /v1/generate with streaming=true and max_tokens=60000.
3) Observe initial portion of tokens stream, then stall; client times out after 90s or receives 504.

Observed behavior:
- Initial generation and stream begin normally for first ~2000 tokens.
- Throughput drops sharply; the worker process shows high CPU on host but low GPU util in some samples.
- KV-cache growth is large (observed footprint ~2.4x compared to expected).
- Request either ends with an HTTP 504 from our edge or a client-side socket timeout depending on retry window.

Expected behavior:
- Streaming should continue at approximately steady token/s rate (subject to model size) until max_tokens reached or generation completes.
- System should fail fast with a descriptive 5xx if a serving constraint is hit rather than silent stalls.

Logs / Traces collected:
- Edge logs: connection held open; upstream returned 504 after 95s for request id rwd-usw-8f3a
- Serving runtime traces: request assigned to worker host gpu-12; kernel execution latency spikes after ~2k tokens, with repeated GC events in process logs.
- KV-cache metrics: memory spike correlating with stall time; cache eviction not keeping up.
- SRE sampling: strace on worker showed repeated futex/wait events consistent with queue backpressure.

Investigation notes / hypotheses so far:
- Hypothesis A: Continuous-batching + very large KV cache leads to runaway per-request memory/serialization overhead; runtime stalls while moving/compacting KV cache.
- Hypothesis B: A path in the streaming controller triggers repeated small wakeups under heavy prefix size (inefficient signaling), delaying downstream flushes to the client.
- Hypothesis C: For some model variants, quantization/attention kernel selection yields pathological perf when sequence length + new generation length exceed internal thresholds, causing CPU fallback paths.
- We observed that when the same request is routed to a lower-batched, dedicated single-worker instance (not autoscaled), the stall is less frequent but still present, suggesting both runtime and routing factors.

Workarounds attempted / recommended to customer:
- Reduce max_tokens to <= 20k or split generation into chunked suffix generations. Customer reports this reduces failures but increases orchestration complexity.
- Temporarily pin routing to a low-batch policy (support-set to route through dedicated single-worker gateway). This reduced incidence in ~70% of test runs.
- Increase client-side socket timeout to 180s as a stopgap (not ideal for UX).

Next steps / action items:
- SRE: capture a full CPU/GPU trace on next reproduced run and enable detailed heap profiling for the worker process (assigned: Maya Chen).
- Runtime team: add instrumentation around KV cache copy/compact/eviction path to measure time spent per request; create a microbenchmark for very long prefix + generation (assigned: Julian Park).
- Routing team: evaluate whether batching window heuristics can be bypassed for requests with explicit large max_tokens flag to avoid batching-induced stalls (assigned: Anika Rao).
- Product: update guidance for customers on recommended max_tokens + prefix sizing and add explicit error if request exceeds safe combined token heuristic (assigned: Priya Narayanan).

Customer communication:
- Customer notified 2026-03-12 (initial report) and informed of workaround options same day.
- We told the customer we expect a preliminary root-cause hypothesis by 2026-03-16 and will follow up with timeline for fixes.

Resolution criteria:
- Repro rate with baseline workload falls below 1% for similar prefix+max_tokens after fixes and/or a clear client-visible error is returned when request exceeds safe limits.
